findings.where: apps/web/components/work/work-detail.tsx:808 (the AC5 trade-invoice link block inside PostedEntrySection)
findings.what: The open item's outstanding amount is interpolated directly as a raw integer of sen (`{tradeInvoice.outstanding_cents}`) instead of being routed through the house currency-display convention. Every other money value in the app renders through apps/web/components/journals/money.tsx's `<Money cents=.../>` (Intl.NumberFormat, style: "currency", currency: "MYR", currencyDisplay: "narrowSymbol") or, in a non-JSX value-prop position, through `formatCents` from lib/journals/balance.ts (the pattern apps/web/components/accruals/accrual-detail.tsx:68 uses for its own amount fact). This block does neither, so a bookkeeper viewing a posted trade invoice's Work page sees the literal string "Outstanding: 106000" instead of "Outstanding: RM 1,060.00" -- easy to misread as roughly 100x the real amount, and not what AC12 means by "exact money ... values".
findings.evidence: git diff origin/main...HEAD -- apps/web/components/work/work-detail.tsx, line 808: `<> · {tti("outstanding")}: {tradeInvoice.outstanding_cents}</>`, with no cents-to-ringgit conversion anywhere in the surrounding JSX (confirmed by direct Read of the file, lines 779-814). money.tsx's own header comment states it replaced a hand-rolled string formatter as "no longer the render path" (N9 review) -- i.e. this IS the documented house convention for rendering money in JSX. No test in the diff catches it: apps/web/e2e/trade-invoice-walk.spec.ts:158 only asserts `expect(page.getByTestId("work-trade-invoice-links")).toContainText(TI.openItemId)` -- it never asserts the outstanding text -- and trade-invoice-form.test.tsx / -a11y / -keyboard never touch work-detail.tsx. reports/655-final.md does not name this as a residual anywhere.
findings.fix: Import `Money` from `@/components/journals/money` (already used elsewhere in the codebase for exactly this shape) and render `<Money cents={tradeInvoice.outstanding_cents} />` in place of the bare number; add a walk or unit assertion on the formatted text so a future regression cannot slip past the same gap.

findings.what: The block's own code comment (lines 768-778) states it names "which kind, which party, which two dates, the exact total, and — once the run posts — the journal entry, the signed open item with its due date and outstanding, and the receipt." The rendered JSX never interpolates `tradeInvoice.total_cents` anywhere, even though the type (apps/web/lib/work/trade-invoice-reads.ts's TradeInvoiceRead.total_cents) carries it and a translation key TradeInvoice.link.total = "Total" was authored for exactly this purpose and is never referenced by any tti(...) call in the diff. For a trade invoice that is `admitted` but not yet `posted` (a real, named state the same comment says must render "the document's facts" rather than blanks), there is no amount visible anywhere else on the Work page either (the journal-lines table only exists once the entry posts), so the invoice's stated total is simply not visible on this page in that state.
findings.evidence: grep -n "total_cents" apps/web/components/work/work-detail.tsx returns no hits inside the rendered block (only the type import at the top of the file). grep -n '"total"' apps/web/messages/en.json shows the key defined at line 1689; no `tti("total"` call exists anywhere in the diff, confirming the key is dead. reports/655-final.md does not name this gap as a residual.
findings.fix: Render `tradeInvoice.total_cents` (via `<Money cents=.../>`) beside documentDate/dueDate in the same block, using the already-authored `total` key, so the comment's own claim becomes true.
